EBT / SNAP

How this works

SNAP covers food you cook at home, so nearly every recipe here qualifies. Some states have extra limits on items like soda and candy. With this on, the app uses your state's rules from your ZIP code, hides recipes with an ingredient your state doesn't allow, and leaves out add-ins that aren't covered. Chocolate chips may count as candy depending on your state, so they're treated as not covered there.

“Per serving” counts only what the recipe uses. “At checkout” is what you'd pay buying whole packages, minus pantry items you have. Prices are BLS regional averages for unless marked otherwise. Your goal

Targets are estimates for healthy adults. If you're pregnant or breastfeeding, have a medical condition, or have had an eating disorder, skip the goal modes and ask your doctor or a registered dietitian. Your details stay on this device unless you turn on sync.

Not sure what to aim for? A registered dietitian or your doctor can set goals that fit you.

Today

    Nutrition values are estimates from the USDA National Nutrient Database (SR28), worked out from each recipe's ingredients. % Daily Value uses the FDA's 2,000-calorie reference. This is general information, not medical advice.

    My stores

    Save the stores you shop at. The one you pick here sets the prices you see.

    VIC member prices are the sale prices every cardholder gets. Personal e-VIC offers and digital coupons loaded to your card aren't included, because they're tied to your own account.

    Add a store

    Live prices are only available for Kroger-family stores right now, so this store uses average prices for your area. You can type exact prices on the Prices tab.

    Use on another device

    Sync keeps your favorites, meal plans, pantry, stores, goals and imported recipes the same on your phone and computer. Anyone with your code can see and change this data, so keep it private like a password.
